chapter: Western University and Kansas City nightlife
title: Geography of the two Kansas Cities and the Hawaiian Gardens
summary: Ramey explains Kansas City, Kansas versus Missouri and where the Hawaiian Gardens stood.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: And we had a chance, you know, to go out into Kansas City. We went to the Hawaiian Gardens; that's right on Independence Avenue, where Independence Avenue runs into that highway that takes you across to north Kansas City.
Just explain to me, since I've never been there--Kansas City, Missouri, Kansas City, Kansas--they are one city?

It's called Greater Kansas City, but they are two individual cities. Kansas City, Kansas is on the Kansas side. It's divided by--well, the Kaw [Kansas] and the Missouri River meets right there, but there's a viaduct that separates Kansas City, Kansas from Kansas, Missouri.
Well, I mean, how far across is it?
I would say as far as from here to 47th Street, I mean to the major part of each city. Yeah.
Yeah, well, I mean it isn't a very big division, is it?
No, well, they call it Greater Kansas City.
Yeah. So I mean you could go back and forth there.
